title: Values, Variables & Types
content: JavaScript has several important data types including string, number, boolean, null, undefined, object and symbol.

title: Functions & Parameters
content: Functions allow you to group reusable logic. A function can receive parameters and return a value.

title: Objects
content: Objects store related information using key-value pairs.

title: Arrays
content: Arrays are ordered collections of values. JavaScript provides methods such as map, filter and reduce.

title: Scope & Closures
content: Scope determines where variables can be accessed. Closures allow functions to remember variables from their surrounding scope.

title: Good Parts
content: Writing maintainable JavaScript involves using clear naming, avoiding unnecessary complexity and understanding the language features you use.

title: Python Basics
content: Python is a high-level programming language known for readable syntax.

title: Functions
content: Python functions are defined using the def keyword.

title: React Basics
content: React is a JavaScript library for building user interfaces using components.

title: Props & State
content: Props allow data to be passed to components. State stores data that can change over time.
